message.reasoning:
Need to ensure file size under 18KB. Let's write it carefully and compactly but still beautiful. Design: - SVG full viewport, viewBox maybe dynamic; easier to use pixel coordinates matching window size and update on resize. Use JS to set width/height and positions. Structure: - defs: water gradient (linearGradient vertical), sand gradient, radial gradients for bubbles, glow filters maybe (filters are fine, inline). - Light rays (caustics) — ambient god rays using polygons with low opacity, slowly animating — gives the scene depth. - Particles (plankton) drifting — extra ambience, but keep count small for file size. - Seafloor: path with rocks, some pebbles, a couple of static rocks. - Seaweed: 3 seaweeds built from stacked ellipses or wavy paths with sway animation (JS rotate or SVG animate transform). Use CSS animation with transform-origin at base and skew/rotate sway. - Two fish: - Fish A: big, roundish/short body (like angelfish), warm orange/coral, with tall triangular dorsal fin, stripes, tail triangular, eye with pupil, mouth curve. - Fish B: small, slender elongated body (like a small blue fish), teal/blue, faster, tail triangular, side fin. - Fish constructed as with primitives; flip horizontally by scale(-1,1) depending on direction. Animation: JS requestAnimationFrame loop moving fish x with wrap-around, bubbles y rising with respawn, seaweed sway maybe CSS keyframes. Tail wiggle: CSS animation on tail group rotate about the joint; fish body bob via CSS translateY. Also subtle rotation from bob. Bubble: circles with highlight — group of circle + small white circle highlight. Recycle DOM nodes. Also small ambient: distant school of tiny fish silhouettes? The requirement says exactly 2 fish — adding silhouettes could violate "exactly 2 fish". So avoid extra fish. Use only particles/plankton and jellyfish? Jellyfish might count as fish? No, but risky — a jellyfish isn't a fish, but the requirement "exactly 2 fish" is about fish. Still, to be safe, skip jellyfish. Use light shafts, particles, and maybe a few distant bubbles. Keep to two fish. Layered background: water gradient, light shafts, caustic surface shimmer at top (wavy path animated), distant rock silhouettes, seafloor, seaweed behind and in front of fish, particles, bubbles, vignette. Typography: the scene is graphics only; but there could be a small label overlay text. The prompt says fish recognizable without a text label. A tasteful HUD could add polish. But careful — "no external assets" means fonts must be system stacks: a display serif like "Didot, 'Playfair Display', 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, serif" for the display face and a clean system sans for the label — no network fetch needed. Keep minimal so it doesn't distract. A tiny corner label is fine and adds polish. I'll add a small corner caption with a live readout of the fish species names — living element. Keep it subtle. Let me make it: bottom-left small block: eyebrow "SVG PRIMITIVES · 2 fish" and a display-line "Pelagic Drift". Also a live readout of bubble count. Keep small. Hmm, keep file under 18KB — that's fine. Implementation details: Use SVG with width="100%" height="100%" and no viewBox — coordinates = pixel space (SVG user units default = px). Actually without viewBox, user units map 1:1 to px. Good; use JS to read innerWidth/innerHeight. Water gradient: from #7ed6f0-ish top to #06182e bottom. "lighter blue near the top, darker blue near the bottom" ✓. Seafloor ~10-15% of viewport height: compute floorY = H * 0.88 (floor band height ~12%). Draw path with undulating top edge. Redraw on resize. Seaweed: create as paths generated in JS (wavy path) with sway via CSS animation with different durations/delays. Rooted at floorY at given x. Use quadratic path built from generated points, plus leaf ellipses. Simpler: build a wavy stem path via cubic segments, stroke thick with round caps and gradient green; plus a few leaf ellipses. Sway: CSS animation transform: rotate small angle with transform-origin at base — need transform-box: fill-box? For SVG transform-origin works with `transform-origin: Xpx Ypx` in CSS (user units) — supported in modern browsers. I'll set style.transformOrigin = `${x}px ${baseY}px`. Actually a nicer sway: apply skewX oscillation. Let's use rotate between -3.5deg and 3.5deg with ease-in-out, plus a slight scaleY breathing. Bubbles: pool of ~26 bubbles. Each has x, y, r, speed, wobble phase. Respawn when y < -r: respawn at random x near seafloor with random r. "smaller bubbles rise faster": speed = base * (0.4 + 1.2/(r*0.1+1))... simpler: v = 28 + 900/r? Let's define speed = (14 + 120 / r) * depthFactor. For r=3 → 54 px/s; r=10 → 26 px/s. Good: smaller faster. Bubble group: circle with fill url(#bubbleFill) radial gradient (white translucent with rim) + highlight small ellipse. To keep DOM cheap, use one . Use per-bubble r on the circle, highlight offset computed. Light shafts: 4 polygons from top with gradient fill (white low alpha), CSS animation of opacity + slight translateX/skew, different durations. Use a group with mix-blend-mode: screen? Keep simple: fill="url(#rayGrad)" with opacity animated. Caustic shimmer at the top: a repeating wave path? Could do 2-3 thin sine paths translating horizontally. Use a path built in JS spanning 2x width, translateX loop. Might be a nice touch. Let's add: top band 0..6% of height with lighter fill and two animated sine strokes with low opacity. Particles: 30 tiny circles drifting slowly, with CSS animations? Do in JS cheaply — but keep code small. Maybe use CSS animations only with random inline styles generated in JS. Simplest: create circles with CSS `animation: drift Xs linear infinite` translating upward — need transform translate. Generate each with random start pos, random duration, keyframes drift from translateY(0) to translateY(-120vh)? That would move off; but they wrap via animation loop. Yes: particle keyframe: 0%{transform:translateY(0);opacity:0} ... 100%{transform:translateY(-H)}. Fine with per-element random x/y set as cx/cy and a CSS animation with translate — but need the wrap; animation restarts so it teleports back — that's fine (opacity fade in/out hides it). Fish design (primitives only): Fish A — "Sunburst Angelfish" — big, deep/round body: - Body: ellipse rx 78, ry 62 (roundish tall), plus maybe a path for a pointed snout. Use ellipse + a teardrop via path for snout? Keep ellipse body and a small triangular snout path. Simpler: body = ellipse rx=76 ry=58. Mouth region at right side (fish drawn facing right in local coords), then group flips via scale. - Tail: triangular polygon points from body rear (-70,0) to (-140,-46) (-140,46)... Actually rear at x = -rx = -76. Tail: path M -66 0 L -136 -44 L -118 0 L -136 44 Z — a nice forked triangle. Requirement says triangular tail; a triangular fork is fine; keep clearly triangular. - Dorsal fin: path on top: M -20 -50 Q 10 -110 60 -44 Z (triangular-ish sail). Anal fin bottom too. - Pectoral fin: small ellipse/triangle at side near (18, 12) rotated, animated slight. - Eye: circle at (40,-14) r 11 white with dark stroke, pupil circle r 5 at (42.5,-13), highlight tiny circle r2 white. "Exactly 1 visible eye" — one eye only ✓ (only draw one). - Mouth: path M 66 12 q 10 6 16 -2 stroke, or a small open shape (path) at snout. - Stripes: 2-3 vertical bands using paths clipped to body (clipPath with body ellipse) — nice. - Colors: warm coral/orange gradient (#ff9a3c → #e05a2b) with yellow fin tips. Fish B — small slender blue fish: - Body: ellipse rx 46 ry 17 (long/slender), scaled. - Tail: triangle from -42,0 to -74,-22 / -74,22. - Dorsal: small triangle path at top; side fin tiny. - Eye near front (28,-4) r 5.5, pupil r 2.6. - Mouth: tiny line/curve. - Colors: teal/cyan with silver belly (#3fd0e0 → #1b6fb0). Both fish groups: containing (scale ±1) containing parts. Tail wiggle: CSS animation on `.tail { transform-origin: ; animation: wiggle }` — but transform-origin per fish differs; set inline via style with the joint in local coords. Since flip group uses scale(-1,1), the wiggle rotation inside is fine. Bob: CSS animation on the fish inner wrapper translateY(±6px) — but the outer transform is set by JS (translate(x,y)). Nest: g.fish (JS transform translate) > g.bob (CSS animation translateY) > g.flip (scale) > parts. Wait CSS animation on .bob with translateY conflicts? .bob only has CSS transform, fine. Tail wiggle rotate: transform-box: fill-box + transform-origin: 100% 50% — for the tail path whose right-most point is the joint. That works nicely and avoids coordinate math. transform-box: fill-box is supported in modern browsers (Chrome 64+, Safari 14+, FF 55+). Good. But Safari support for transform-box on SVG... it's supported since Safari 14. Acceptable. Fallback: also set transform-origin in user-space? Can't do both. Use fill-box; fine. Pectoral fin flap similar with transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 0% 0%? For a fin rooted at its left tip. Set origin accordingly per element class. Seaweed sway: JS-built group, set style.transformOrigin in px user units (works with default transform-box view-box). Good. Foreground: a couple of dark rocks in front, and one seaweed in front of fish (z-order: floor back, seaweed back, fish, seaweed front, rocks front, bubbles top). Also vignette rect with radialGradient overlay for depth. Resize handling: recompute W,H, floor path, seaweed positions, fish y positions. Fish y positions: big fish at ~45% of H, small at ~28%. Keep within water column above floor. Speeds: big fish 34 px/s, small 96 px/s — noticeably different. Small fish faster and opposite direction to add life. Wrap-around: if facing right (dir=+1) and x > W + margin → x = -margin. Direction: fish A moves right (dir +1, flip scale x = 1... drawn facing right by default so scale 1). Fish B moves left: draw facing right and apply scale(-1,1), x decreasing; wrap when x < -margin → W+margin. Add subtle vertical sinusoidal drift per fish in JS: y = baseY + sin(t*f)*amp. Also add tail speed tied to fish speed for coherence (CSS durations: slow fish 1.4s, fast 0.45s). Readout HUD: small element bottom-left with a monospace label showing "big · 34 px/s" updating? Could show live x position — a living element. Keep light: two lines listing the two residents and their speeds with a little animated indicator. Use system font stacks. Also mouse interaction: fish don't react to mouse, keep simple — maybe bubbles spawn at cursor click? Nice micro-interaction: click anywhere to release a burst of bubbles. That's a lovely touch and cheap. Add: pointerdown → spawn 6 bubbles at that x,y. Also cursor: crosshair? Keep default. I'll add subtle. Let's also add hover on fish: pointer-events on fish groups, on hover pause? Might be gimmicky but adds interactivity. Simpler: on hover, fish speeds up slightly (a dart) with CSS class — implement with mouseenter/mouseleave adding class that changes CSS animation-duration... speed change needs JS: multiply target speed and ease back. Nice micro-interaction: `fish.dart = 1` decays to 0. pointerenter sets dart = 2.2. Implement. Let's write the code, keeping size in check. Aim ~12-15KB. ...
``` Note: SVG without viewBox → 1 user unit = 1 px ✓. Defs: - `gWater` linearGradient x1=0 y1=0 x2=0 y2=1: stops: 0% #86e0f2? Let's do: 0 #7fdcf2, 22% #3aa9d6, 55% #16608f, 80% #0a3358, 100% #041829. - `gSand`: 0 #f2dcae → 40% #c9a166 → 100% #6d4d2e. - `gRay`: linear top→bottom white .22 → transparent. - `gA` body, `gFinA`, `gB` body, `gFinB`. - `bubFill` radialGradient: 25% offset white .30 alpha, 80% rgba(200,240,255,.06), 100% rgba(255,255,255,.45)? Radial gradient with focal offset for glassy look: fx=.35 fy=.3. - `gVig` radial for vignette: center transparent → edges rgba(2,10,20,.55). Use radialGradient with r=.75 cx=.5 cy=.42 stops rgba(0,0,0,0) → rgba(2,12,22,.6). - `gRock`, `gKelpA`, `gKelpB`, `gHill`. - `gDeep` for the hill silhouette. Filter: a soft glow filter for the rays and maybe the surface — `` applied to ray group. Blur over full-screen might be costly but ok. Use stdDeviation 12. Rays without blur look hard-edged; blur is nicer. Apply filter to ray group (single filter region). Might be heavy on large screens at 60fps... The rays are static (CSS animating opacity + slow translate) → re-blurs per frame. Risk of jank. Alternative: pre-soften rays by using gradient fills horizontally? Use fewer rays with linear gradient fill that has soft alpha at the edges — can't do per-polygon edge softness with a single gradient... but I can give each ray a horizontal linearGradient (x1=0,x2=1 with transparent → white → transparent across the ray bbox) — that gives soft lateral edges! Combine with vertical fade gradient. Two gradients: use the ray shape filled with horizontal soft gradient and set group opacity fading downward via a mask... Simpler: use a `` filled with vertical gradient as a mask on a group of laterally-soft rays. Or simply: each ray polygon filled with a horizontal-soft gradient, and add a full-screen rect with the vertical depth gradient in `mask`. Let's do mask: `` where gDepthMask goes white at top to black at ~75%. Apply mask="url(#mDepth)" to the rays group. Good, no filters. Cost: one mask, fine. Similarly a glow for bubbles? skip. Let's write CSS animations: ```css @keyframes sway{0%,100%{transform:rotate(-3deg)}50%{transform:rotate(3.4deg)}} @keyframes bob{0%,100%{transform:translateY(-6px)}50%{transform:translateY(7px)}} @keyframes wig{0%,100%{transform:rotate(-10deg)}50%{transform:rotate(10deg)}} @keyframes flap{0%,100%{transform:rotate(-8deg)}50%{transform:rotate(12deg)}} @keyframes rise{from{transform:translateY(0)}to{transform:translateY(-108vh)}} @keyframes surf{from{transform:translateX(0)}to{transform:translateX(-160px)}} @keyframes glow{0%,100%{opacity:.10}50%{opacity:.30}} @keyframes huddot{0%,100%{opacity:.35;transform:scale(.8)}50%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1.25)}} ``` Fish B bob duration shorter (2.4s) via inline style animation-duration. HUD CSS: ```css .hud{position:fixed;left:26px;bottom:26px;z-index:5;pointer-events:none; font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;max-width:min(46vw,340px)} .hud .title{font-family:var(--display);font-size:clamp(26px,3.4vw,44px);letter-spacing:0;text-transform:none;font-style:italic;line-height:.95;font-weight:400;color:#f2fbff;text-shadow:0 2px 24px rgba(3,20,40,.7)} ``` Strong type contrast: big display italic + tiny mono uppercase ✓. ``` Bars animate width via JS reflecting dart boost. Nice living element. Hmm, species names should be plausible-ish Latin. Use "Helicolenus robustus" & "Caesio celerrima"? Fine, invented.
